core.title: Reach sibling features of the shared tree only through the layer root
core.given: A module inside one feature directory of the shared tree (the tree of code shared across features, where each feature directory is nested under a layer)
core.when: it imports a capability of a sibling feature of the shared tree
core.then: The import MUST go through the layer root, never directly into the sibling feature's internals.
prefer: Reuse an export that already represents the required capability.
If the capability is intentionally shared, expose the smallest stable surface from the layer root.
If it is not a shared responsibility, keep the implementation local instead of reaching across.
avoid: Importing a path inside a sibling feature's directory.
Creating a generic shared module merely to make the import legal.
unless: Test files and vendored/build trees are never scanned.
Imports that resolve outside the project graph (external-package specifiers, per the profile's external-import idiom) are not layer-checked.
A file with no layer segment (no role assigned, per the profile's assignment) is outside these rules rather than in violation of them.
core.why: A feature's internals are its own; the layer root is the surface it deliberately exposes. Reaching past it couples two features through a path neither chose to publish, which is how a shared module quietly becomes unsplittable.
evidence: The cross-feature dependency goes through the intended public boundary (the layer root); this rule's architecture check reports no finding.
verification: Resolve each import of a module inside a feature directory of the shared tree and flag one whose resolved target sits inside a different feature directory of the shared tree.
Term shared feature: one feature directory of the shared tree (shape from the profile); its internals belong to it alone.
Term layer root: the surface a feature deliberately exposes; cross-feature use goes through it, or two features are coupled through a path neither published.
The observer resolves every import of every in-scope module (pre-existing or newly added/changed) and is not limited to diff edits.
Test files and vendored/build trees are never scanned; the exact excluded classification is the stack-wide never-scanned list owned by the stack's checker (profile roots.excluded).
Do not layer-check imports that resolve outside the project graph (per the profile's external-import idiom).
Files with no layer segment (no role assigned, per the profile's assignment) are out of scope, not violations.

values: module inside a feature directory of the shared tree
cross-feature import finding emitted by this rule's architecture check

fires: A module inside one feature directory of the shared tree adds an import resolving to a file inside a different feature directory's internals.
A module inside one feature directory of the shared tree already contains (unchanged) an import resolving into another feature's internals.
An existing shared-tree module's import is retargeted from the layer root to a path inside a sibling feature directory.
doesNotFire: A shared-tree feature module imports another feature's capability through the layer root.
A module imports a file inside its own feature directory.
A test file or a file in a vendored/build tree imports a sibling feature's internals.
An import uses a bare external-package specifier (resolves outside the project graph).
The importing file has no layer segment in its path.

profileRequirements.meaning: Where the shared-across-features tree lives and how it nests (layer, then feature); the rule scopes modules inside one feature directory of this tree.
How a file is assigned to a layer (role) for this check, and that a file with no layer segment is out of scope rather than a violation.
profileRequirements.bunValue: the layer segment of the file's path; a file with no layer segment is out of scope, not a violation

profileRequirements.meaning: How an import that resolves outside the project graph is recognised, so that it is excluded from the layer check.
profileRequirements.bunValue: bare npm specifiers (resolve outside the project graph)

profileRequirements.meaning: The stack-wide never-scanned list; test files and these trees are outside the check's scope, with the exact classification owned by the stack's checker.

neutralityNotes: The obligation itself is stack-neutral; only observer encodings are Bun-specific (the path glob and the detector/finding id, both in bunOnly). 'Bare npm specifier' is generalized to 'imports resolving outside the project graph' with the Bun idiom carried by profile idiom.external_import. The term 'layer root' is defined only conceptually in bun.json (the surface a feature deliberately exposes) with no concrete module path, so the core carries the conceptual definition and each realization pins the concrete surface itself. The closed fact-type vocabulary has no path/location fact, so the scope fact is expressed as a role-level fact.
